12,12-diethyl-Aplog1 (3), a derivative of Aplog1, is a superior anti-tumor promoter and anti-proliferation agent than the natural product Aplog-1 and its 11,11-dimethyl derivative.
12,12- dimethyl-Aplog1 is a superior derivative that inhibits cancer cell growth and binds to protein kinase C δ, a putative target protein, with higher affinity than Aplog- 1.
the 12, 12-dimethyl derivative of Aplog -1 (3), which is an analog of the tumor-promoting phorbol esters, inhibits tumor promotion and cancer cell growth more potently than the parent Aplog-1.

the synthesis and biological evaluation of the 12-12-dimethyl derivative of Aplog1, an anti-proliferation agent that inhibits tumor promotion and cancer cell growth by binding to protein kinase Cd.
the development of novel anti-tumor agents based on the structure of aplysiatoxins.
the development of novel anti-cancer drugs from marine natural products, with an emphasis on the discovery of novel anti-tumor-promoting agents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 12, 12-dimethyl group is a useful structural element for the design of anti-cancer drugs, and that 3 is an attractive candidate for further development as a lead for anti-carcinogenic agents.

the local hydrophobic character around the spiro-ketal moiety of 12,12,13,13-tetramethyl-1-hydroxymethylenespiro[4.5]decane-8-one (Aplog-1) is an important structural feature that contributes to its potent anti-proliferation activity.
a hydrophobic group proximal to the 12-position of the aplysiatoxins, which are tumor promoters, is a key structural feature for the conversion of tumor promoters to anti-proliferatives.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the hydrophobicity of a small molecule can be fine-tuned by the introduction of a hydrophobic moiety to improve its biological activities.
a local hydrophobic modification can improve the potency of a natural product.
